metadata.title: NASA Fire Risk Matrix Simulation - Apollo 13
metadata.description: Simulated evolution of fire risk categories across Apollo 13 mission timeline based on NASA 5x4 Risk Matrix. Each data point samples fire hazard type, severity, likelihood, and sensor readings at a given mission elapsed time (MET).

severity_scale.label: Critical
severity_scale.description: Severe injury, major system damage, mission abort

key_events.event: CM Odyssey powered up - emergency proc

fire_hazard_type_descriptions.ELECTRICAL_ARC: Electrical spark or arc causing ignition in spacecraft environment
fire_hazard_type_descriptions.OXYGEN_ENRICHED_COMBUSTION: Fire in pure or enriched O2 atmosphere - extreme burn rate
fire_hazard_type_descriptions.CRYOGENIC_FUEL_LEAK: Leaked cryogenic propellant contacting ignition source
fire_hazard_type_descriptions.PYROTECHNIC_IGNITION: Planned or unplanned activation of explosive ordnance
fire_hazard_type_descriptions.WIRING_INSULATION_BURN: Teflon or wiring insulation burning in O2 environment
fire_hazard_type_descriptions.PRESSURE_VESSEL_RUPTURE_FIRE: Pressurized vessel failure followed by combustion

pre_launch_known_defects.description: Manufacturing defects and pre-launch errors that caused the explosion — from Apollo 13 Review Board Report

defects.description: Thermostatic switches in O2 Tank 2 were spec'd for 28V DC but ground support equipment at KSC applied 65V DC during pre-flight testing on March 27, 1969 — this burned out the switches.
A fill tube assembly was improperly removed from the tank during Beech Aircraft rework in 1965 and incorrectly reinstalled — this prevented proper draining of oxygen during ground tests.

Because Tank 2 would not drain properly during pre-launch tests, engineers used the heater to boil off the residual oxygen for 8 hours at 65V — this further damaged the Teflon insulation on internal wiring.
The damaged wiring insulation was invisible to pre-flight inspection — it only became a fire hazard when the fans were activated in a pure O2 environment during the mission.

mappings.real_mechanism: Teflon insulation on fan motor wiring burned in pure O2 atmosphere inside Tank 2
mappings.nasa_finding: Defect D-03 and D-04 combined to create an ignition source

mappings.real_mechanism: Tank interior was 100% pure gaseous O2 at 880 psi — any ignition source causes explosive combustion
mappings.nasa_finding: Normal materials become highly flammable in this environment (even Teflon)

mappings.real_mechanism: Tank 2 structural failure at 1008.3 psi blew off Bay 4 panel and ruptured Tank 1 supply lines
mappings.nasa_finding: Physical impulse of 0.4 ft/sec Delta-V measured on spacecraft at moment of rupture
